title: Ask More, Hear Less: How a Review Prompt Changes What Online Ratings Show
abstract: arXiv:2611.02623v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Platforms ask customers for online reviews to reduce self-selection, but theory conflicts on whether review solicitation makes online ratings more or less informative. Selection theory implies that asking helps, voice theory that it dilutes the news, and research on rating inflation that compression destroys information. We reconcile these views with signal detection theory, which separates what a rating knows (its sensitivity) from what it shows (its criterion). We test the framework on Steam, a leading PC video game store, whose client began in October 2019 to prompt players for a review after about three hours of play. Using a difference-in-discontinuities design at that inferred threshold in 21.6 million Steam reviews of 315 games, we find that review counts just above the threshold become 4.25 times those just below, and the jump in the positive share grows by 6.6 percentage points. Agreement with critics changes little near launc

translated_title: 问得更多，听得更少：评论提示如何改变在线评分所呈现的信息
translated_abstract: 平台邀请客户撰写在线评论以减少自我选择偏差，但理论界对于评论征集究竟是让在线评分信息更丰富还是更贫乏存在分歧：选择理论认为主动询问有帮助，发声理论认为这会稀释真实信息，而关于评分通胀的研究则认为压缩会破坏信息含量。我们借助信号检测理论调和了这些观点，该理论将评分“知道什么”（敏感性）与评分“显示什么”（判定标准）区分开来。我们在Steam——一家领先的PC游戏商店——上检验这一框架，其客户端于2019年10月开始在玩家游玩约三小时后提示其撰写评论。利用对315款游戏的2160万条Steam评论在该推断阈值处采用的双重差分断点设计，我们发现阈值上方的评论数量是阈值下方的4.25倍，且正面评分占比的跃升增加了6.6个百分点；而与专业评论家的契合度在上线初期变化不大。
tldr: 该研究利用Steam在2019年10月于玩家游玩约三小时后主动提示撰写评论这一自然实验，发现该提示使评论数量增至4.25倍并推高正面评分占比6.6个百分点，表明主动征集评论虽然大幅增加了评论数量，却让评分变得更加正面、稀释了评分所传递的信息。
en_tdlr: Exploiting Steam's October 2019 review prompt after roughly three hours of play as a natural experiment, this study shows the prompt multiplied review counts by 4.25 and raised the positive rating share by 6.6 percentage points, indicating that soliciting reviews boosts review volume but makes ratings more positive and less informative.
